title: Federal Funding
description: Federal funding plays a crucial role in supporting universities and research institutions across the United States. In fiscal year 2023, approximately $60 billion was allocated from the federal government to universities. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is a significant contributor, with over 80% of its funding directed towards grants at universities and hospitals. However, funding challenges persist, as seen with the Trump administration's cancellation of $900 million in IES contracts and the freezing of $790 million in funding for Northwestern University.

representative_facts.fact_content: Roughly $60 billion flowed from the federal government to universities in fiscal year 2023
More than 80% of NIH funding goes to grants at universities and hospitals
The Trump administration canceled $900 million in IES contracts

title: Federal Funding
description: Federal funding cuts have significantly impacted educational and scientific research institutions. Approximately $1 billion in federal contracts for education research were cancelled, and over $17.5 million in funding was withdrawn by federal agencies. Prestigious universities like MIT and Johns Hopkins rely heavily on federal funds, with up to 48% of their revenue coming from these sources. The University of Alabama at Birmingham received over $400 million from the NIH in 2022, highlighting the critical role of federal support in sustaining research activities.

representative_facts.fact_content: Cancellation of $1 billion in federal education research contracts
MIT received 48% of its funding from the federal government in 2022–23
UAB received more than $400 million in funding from NIH in 2022

title: Federal Cuts
description: Significant reductions in federal funding are impacting various educational and research institutions across the U.S. The Federal Work-Study program faces a $980 million cut, while the University of Massachusetts Amherst anticipates a $6 million loss. The NIH has terminated or delayed over 2,000 grant awards, affecting numerous projects and staff. These cuts are part of broader budget reductions affecting public research, climate research, and health institutions.

title: Federal Funding
description: Several universities in the U.S. are experiencing significant changes in federal funding. Conversely, Northwestern University faced a freeze on $790 million in funding, and the University of Pennsylvania saw a $175 million reduction in its research budget. These shifts highlight the varying impacts of federal funding decisions on higher education institutions.

title: Federal Funding
description: Federal funding cuts, particularly from the NIH, are impacting research institutions significantly. Proposed caps on indirect funding cuts are set at 15%, with the NIH having already canceled over $3 billion in grants. These cuts could result in an annual economic loss of $16 billion and the loss of approximately 68,000 jobs. Prestigious universities, which rely heavily on federal funds, are particularly affected, with institutions like Johns Hopkins University receiving substantial federal support.

representative_facts.fact_content: The NIH has cancelled well over $3 billion in grants
Cuts would lead to about $16 billion in economic loss annually
Cuts would lead to around 68,000 lost jobs annually
